facts_of_case: The parties are the wife and husband. The wife has sought to transfer a divorce petition filed by her husband to another court. During pendency of the transfer petition, the parties arrived at a settlement and have decided to dissolve their marriage by mutual consent.

legal_principles.principle: Parties can settle their disputes and seek dissolution of marriage by mutual consent.
legal_principles.held: They have indeed arrived at a settlement and have decided to part ways and hence, have filed an application under Article 142 of the Constitution seeking dissolution of their marriage by a decree of divorce by mutual consent.

legal_principles.principle: Parties can quash pending proceedings in accordance with their settlement agreement.
legal_principles.held: The parties have sought for quashing of certain proceedings initiated by them inter se which are mentioned in paragraph ‘2’ of the Settlement Agreement.

outcome.final_order: The parties' joint application for dissolution of their marriage by decree of divorce by mutual consent is allowed. The couple's minor son will be in the custody of the wife, and the husband has paid a settlement amount to the wife.

keywords: Latin Maxim: Nemo judex in causa sua
use_for_drafting: drafting a transfer petition under Section 25 CPC
advising on divorce proceedings under Hindu Marriage Act
negotiating settlement agreements in family law disputes
